subject: Security architecture packet for Dedicated/Private — topology & evidence
messages:
From: David Lin <david.lin@acme-corp.com>
To: chloe_martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
Cc: kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Request: topology + isolation details for SOC 2 / SIG / CAIQ review

Hi Chloe,

We're starting our SIG and SOC 2 evidence collection for the ACME integration and need a clear security architecture packet for Redwood's Dedicated and Private deployment modes. The auditor and our engineering security team asked for the following items (minimum):

- High-level network boundary diagram that shows control plane vs data plane, with annotated hops for a sample request path (ingress -> routing -> model-serving pods -> egress).
- Explicit control-plane isolation notes (management API, key rotation, audit logging path).
- KMS boundaries and when customer-managed keys vs Redwood KMS are used in Private mode.
- Egress controls, NATing strategy, and examples of per-tenant egress IPs / SNAT behaviour.
- Confirmation of VPC peering, transit gateway, or private link options and any required IAM roles.
- Evidence/artifacts: one diagram (PNG), a short narrative, and one table showing controls mapped to SIG/CAT/OSL questions.

Can you confirm whether you can provide this by EOD Thu (2026-01-15)? Also let me know if you prefer we send a more formal questionnaire or a template.

Thanks,
David
David Lin
Security Program Manager, Acme Corp
security@acme-corp.com

- For KMS: do you need a statement of support for customer-managed KMS in Private (yes/offline HSM options) or just the default Redwood-managed KMS behavior?

Planned deliverables (we'll attach PNG/PDF + a small spreadsheet mapping controls):
- controlplane_topology (annotated PNG)

- egress_and_kms_boundary_notes (PDF)

I can run a 30-minute walkthrough on Thu morning (09:00-11:00 PST) or Thu afternoon (13:00-15:00 PST). Which works for your team?

Subject: Re: Request: topology + isolation details for SOC 2 / SIG / CAIQ review

Thanks — a couple of internal asks so the packet is audit-ready: 

1) Please include a short sequence diagram (PNG) that shows the following interactions for Dedicated and Private: request ingress -> route selection -> model worker (with KV cache hit/miss callouts) -> control-plane calls for key lookup/metrics upload. The auditor often wants to see the key lookup path separated from the data path.

2) In the isolation matrix, call out whether we rely on tenant-specific subnets, security groups, or namespace-level network policies for enforcement. For Private, add the customer-facing KMS option and a short note on BYOK procedures (what we request from customers during onboarding).

3) Add a short attestation paragraph about logging retention for control-plane audit logs (where they are stored, retention window, and who has access). A 1–2 line bullet is fine.

4) Ensure the attachment filenames are stable (include version numbers). The SOC/third-party process prefers explicit versioning.

If you want, I can review a draft Wed afternoon.

-Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Director, Security Architecture
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Request: topology + isolation details for SOC 2 / SIG / CAIQ review

David — attaching the packet per your ask. Notes below and delivery items are in the Drive folder linked. 

Delivery summary (attached):
- redwood_controlplane_topology_v2.drawio.png — annotated topology showing control-plane vs data-plane with explicit key lookup path and audit-log flow (versioned).
- dedicated_private_isolation_matrix_v1.xlsx — matrix mapping controls to SIG and CAIQ questions, enforcement mechanism (subnet/security-group/namespace policy), and evidence references.
- egress_and_kms_boundary_notes.pdf — short narrative on KMS modes (Redwood-managed, BYOK customer KMS in Private, HSM options) and egress/SNAT patterns.
- soc2_sig_caioq_summary.txt — 2-page plain-text summary auditors like to include with packages.

Key assertions (short):
- Control and data planes are logically separated; control-plane APIs only accessible from management subnets with strict ACLs and mutual TLS.
- Customer BYOK is supported in Private; keys never leave KMS during signing—Redwood holds wrapped DEKs in secure storage when using customer keys.
- Egress granularization: Dedicated pools support per-tenant ephemeral egress IPs documented in the matrix; Private supports customer-managed NAT/proxy configurations per onboarding.
- Audit logs for control-plane are forwarded to a write-once storage with 1 year default retention; access is role-based and logged.

Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2cDEF-example-Redwood-Acme
HubSpot record: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/ACME-5421

Attachments included in this thread: redwood_controlplane_topology_v2.drawio.png, dedicated_private_isolation_matrix_v1.xlsx, egress_and_kms_boundary_notes.pdf, soc2_sig_caioq_summary.txt

If you and your auditor want a quick walkthrough, Thu 09:00 PST tomorrow or Fri 11:00 PST work for me — happy to demo the diagrams and answer sig-level questions.

Best regards,
Chloe Martin
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
